items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: And I later got to meet Spencer Clark who replaced Adrian in the California Ramblers

ctx.x: Exactly. How big is big? So I finally found a fellow who — he was a string bass, tuba and bass sax — he was almost what I eventually became, and he had it in his attic and brought it out and it was completely — it was a silver sax at one point but it was completely black, like somebody spray painted it. Completely tarnished. And he sold it to me for 95 dollars. So I got it, I cleaned it up and brought it into the music store where I was working and it was part of my project to put it together and re-pad it. It…

bigger and bigger, it’s getting closer to a bass mouthpiece, as I’m getting them made bigger, but it’s much easier to find reeds and to control the horn. So that’s pretty much how I got into it. And I would cut classes in high school and take lessons with the other guys who were saxophone players. The teacher wouldn’t — he said you’re busy enough with the tuba and the bass. So the kids taught me how to play the fingerings and stuff and I’m pretty much self-taught on the thing and I read it in treble clef and you…
